To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bariatric surgery is associated with an overall reduction in the incidence of cancer, and that this effect is most pronounced for obesity-related cancers, including cancers of the colon, rectum, esophagus, pancreas, and kidney.
The incidence rate of benign, premalignant, and malignant lesions is high in patients undergoing bariatric surgery, and the incidence rates are higher in patients with a higher BMI.

The most common benign tumors in the bariatric surgery patients are lipomas, followed by leiomyomas, and fibroadenomas; the most common malignant tumors are melanoma and breast cancer; and the most common premalignant lesions in the bariatricsurgery patients are actinic keratoses, followed by dysplastic nevi and squamous cell carcinomas.
